errors: The inductive system cannot consist only of the fundamental groupoids of the strata with naive maps between them. For a closed stratification, the gluing data are carried by deleted tubular neighbourhoods (links): maps π1(link) → π1(stratum) and π1(link) → π1(open stratum). The correct diagram is a homotopy colimit (or exit-path/stratified diagram) including these link groupoids. The fact that these links are themselves K(π,1)'s for M̄_{g,n} (torus bundles over strata) is an additional input. He adds 'et voisinages tubulaires correspondants' as an insertion, partly acknowledging this.

'Lim' must be understood as homotopy colimit, not ordinary colimit of groupoids. Gluing along closed (rather than open) pieces requires a regularity hypothesis (conical/homotopically stratified, local triviality of normal structure). §2 explicitly defers such hypotheses.
The K(π,1) property holds for strata of M̄_{g,n} only as orbifolds/stacks, not for the coarse spaces. His hedge 'quelle que soit leur nature précise' leaves this open.

ideas.what: Homotopy type of a glued (recollement) topos is the homotopy colimit of homotopy types of the pieces
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy colimit decomposition / van Kampen–Segal theorem for homotopy types of topoi; descent for étale homotopy types
ideas.usually_credited_to: Segal (1968, classifying spaces and hocolims), Bousfield–Kan (1972), Lurie (HTT, Seifert–van Kampen for ∞-topoi)
ideas.where_published: Spirit present in Pursuing Stacks (1983) and Les Dérivateurs; no precise statement known to me

ideas.what: Homotopy type of a stratified space with K(π,1) strata is determined by a finite diagram of fundamental groupoids of strata (and links)
ideas.modern_name: Stratified homotopy hypothesis / exit-path category; hocolim decomposition over the stratification poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: MacPherson (exit paths, unpublished c.1990s), Treumann (2009), Lurie (Higher Algebra A.6), Ayala–Francis–Tanaka, Barwick–Glasman–Haine
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses the stratified Teichmüller tower and tubular neighbourhoods but not this homotopy-colimit formula explicitly

ideas.what: Application to Teichmüller moduli spaces and their compactifications (stratified by boundary strata, each a K(π,1) for mapping class groups)
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy type of the Deligne–Mumford stack M̄_{g,n} as a hocolim of classifying spaces of mapping class groups over the category of stable graphs
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ebert–Giansiracusa, 'On the homotopy type of the Deligne–Mumford compactification' (AGT 2008); related work on π1 of M̄_{g,n} by Boggi–Pikaart
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, 'jeu de Lego') is the closest

ideas.what: Simplicial formalism of a closed, locally finite, poset-indexed family of subspaces (X_{Δ0} = ⊔X_i, ...), announced here and begun on the next page
ideas.modern_name: Nerve/Čech construction for poset-indexed closed covers; hocolim over poset

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly proposes (c. early 1980s) computing the homotopy type of Teichmüller modular spaces, their compactifications and tubular neighbourhoods as a finite homotopy colimit of the strata's fundamental (mapping-class) groupoids. This anticipates both the Ebert–Giansiracusa hocolim description of M̄_{g,n} (2008) and the exit-path/stratified homotopy formalism. It links his 'topos stratifié' programme to the Esquisse's Teichmüller tower in homotopy-theoretic rather than Galois-theoretic terms. This specific link appears not to be credited to him.
missed.quote: les espaces modulaires de Teichmüller et leurs compactifiés, et leurs sous-espaces et voisinages tubulaires correspondants ... le type d'homotopie doit pouvoir s'exprimer en termes d'un système inductif convenable (le plus souvent à ensemble d'indices fini) de groupoïdes fondamentaux desdites pièces.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority for the stratified-homotopy viewpoint on moduli of curves. It also suggests running this hocolim decomposition at the level of étale/profinite homotopy types of M̄_{g,n} over Q, which would make it Galois-equivariant (Grothendieck–Teichmüller). That is less developed than the topological version.

deep.surprise_reason: The general principle is standard homotopy-colimit theory, and Grothendieck himself calls it 'relativement triviale'. The explicit early application to Teichmüller spaces, their compactifications and tubular neighbourhoods anticipates later published work (Ebert–Giansiracusa; exit-path formalisms) and ties the stratified-topos notes to the Esquisse. It is a mild, interesting historical precedent rather than a missed theorem.
